answer.text:
### Source, Version, and Scope

* **User-supplied facts:** The query asks for the rule for grenades.
* **Established in tools:** The rules for the Stratagem **GRENADE** retrieved from two sources:
  1. **Core Rules (10th Edition)** [Core Rules p. 42]
  2. **Database record** [DB: stratagems] (publication and edition are not recorded)

---

### 1. Core Rules (10th Edition)

**Citation:** [Core Rules p. 42]  
**Category:** Core – Wargear Stratagem  
**Cost:** 1 CP  

* **WHEN:** Your Shooting phase.
* **TARGET:** One Grenades unit from your army that is not within Engagement Range of any enemy units and has not been selected to shoot this phase.
* **EFFECT:** Select one enemy unit that is not within Engagement Range of any units from your army and is within 8" of and visible to your Grenades unit. Roll six D6: for each 4+, that enemy unit suffers 1 mortal wound.

---

### 2. Database Record

**Citation:** [DB: stratagems]  
**Publication and Edition:** Not recorded  
**Category:** Core – Wargear Stratagem  
**Cost:** 1 CP  

* **WHEN:** Your Shooting phase.
* **TARGET:** One GRENADES unit from your army (excluding units that Advanced, Fell Back or have shot this turn) that is not within Engagement Range of one or more enemy units.
* **EFFECT:** Select one GRENADES model in your unit and one enemy unit that is not within Engagement Range of any units from your army and is within 8" of and visible to your GRENADES model. Roll six D6: for each 4+, that enemy unit suffers 1 mortal wound.

---

### Material Comparison of Sources

* **Cost & Timing:** Both sources require 1 CP and have identical timing (`WHEN: Your Shooting phase`).
* **Target Restrictions:**
  * *[Core Rules p. 42]* restricts the target to a Grenades unit from your army that is not within Engagement Range of any enemy units and has not been selected to shoot this phase.
  * *[DB: stratagems]* explicitly excludes units that Advanced, Fell Back, or have shot this turn, in addition to requiring that the unit is not within Engagement Range of one or more enemy units.
* **Effect Determination (Measurement and Visibility):**
  * *[Core Rules p. 42]* measures distance and visibility from the **Grenades unit** (the selected enemy unit must be within 8" of and visible to your Grenades unit).
  * *[DB: stratagems]* requires selecting one **GRENADES model** in your unit, measuring distance and line of sight from that specific model (the enemy unit must be within 8" of and visible to your GRENADES model).
* **Mortal Wounds:** Both sources resolve the damage identically: roll six D6; for each 4+, the chosen enemy unit suffers 1 mortal wound.

---

### Supported Conclusion and Evidence Gap

* **Conclusion:** Using the Grenade Stratagem costs 1 CP in your Shooting phase to target an eligible friendly unit with the Grenades keyword not in Engagement Range. An eligible enemy unit within 8" and line of sight (not in Engagement Range of any friendly units) suffers 1 mortal wound per roll of 4+ on six D6.
* **Evidence Gap:** The publication name, update document, and edition for the database record [DB: stratagems] are not recorded in the database, so the exact publication context that modified the unit-versus-model targeting and Advance/Fall Back exclusions cannot be identified from these records alone.

[Core Rules p. 42] (page footer p. 42: CORE RULES | STRATAGEMS)
Section: GRENADE
1CP

CORE - WARGEAR STRATAGEM

Priming their hand-held projectiles, these warriors draw back and hurl death into the enemy's midst.

WHEN: Your Shooting phase.

TARGET: One Grenades unit from your army that is not within Engagement Range of any enemy units and has not been selected to shoot this phase.

EFFECT: Select one enemy unit that is not within Engagement Range of any units from your army and is within 8" of and visible to your Grenades unit. Roll six D6: for each 4+, that enemy unit suffers 1 mortal wound.

[Core Rules p. 45] (page footer p. 45: CORE RULES | TERRAIN FEATURES)
Section: CRATERS AND RUBBLE
Many battlefields bear the scars of heavy and sustained bombardment.

[Core Rules p. 10] (page footer p. 10: CORE RULES | THE BATTLE ROUND)
Figure label: COMMAND PHASE
Section: THE BATTLE ROUND > SHOOTING PHASE
Your units fire their ranged weapons at the foe.

[Core Rules p. 26] (page footer p. 26: CORE RULES | WEAPON ABILITIES)
Section: BLAST
High-explosives can fell several warriors in a single blast, but firing them where your comrades will get caught in the ensuing detonation is simply unwise.

Weapons with [BLAST] in their profile are known as Blast weapons, and they make a random number of attacks. Each time you determine how many attacks are made with a Blast weapon, add 1 to the result for every five models that were in the target unit when you selected it as the target (rounding down). Blast weapons can never be used to make attacks against a unit that is within Engagement Range of one or more units from the attacking model's army (including its own unit).

Example: If a weapon with the [BLAST] ability and an Attacks characteristic of 2D6 targets a unit that contains 11 models, and the roll to determine how many attacks are made is a 9, a total of 11 attacks would be made against that unit.

- Add 1 to the Attacks characteristic for every five models in the target unit (rounding down).
- Can never be used against a target that is within Engagement Range of any units from the attacking model's army (including its own).

[Core Rules p. 45] (page footer p. 45: CORE RULES | TERRAIN FEATURES)
Section: CRATERS AND RUBBLE > BENEFIT OF COVER
Each time a ranged attack is allocated to an Infantry model that is wholly on top of this terrain feature, that model has the Benefit of Cover against that attack.

KEYWORDS: Area Terrain, Crater

[Core Rules p. 55]
Section: STRIKE FORCE
| Points per Army   | 2000          |
|-------------------|---------------|
| Duration          | Up to 3 hours |

[Core Rules p. 45] (page footer p. 45: CORE RULES | TERRAIN FEATURES)
Section: CRATERS AND RUBBLE > VISIBILITY
Normal visibility rules apply.

[Core Rules p. 46] (page footer p. 46: CORE RULES | TERRAIN FEATURES)
Section: BATTLEFIELD DEBRIS AND STATUARY > VISIBILITY
Normal visibility rules apply.
